title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation
abstract: arXiv:2611.09785v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: External lexical resources can help large language models (LLMs) translate texts in low-resource languages and specialized domains, but these resources may conflict with models' prior lexical knowledge. To isolate this conflict, we construct a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation task in which familiar source words are assigned new meanings within and across semantic categories. We treat these prompt-supplied meanings as contextual knowledge (CK) and systematically evaluate the effects of word frequency, sentence context, and prompt framing on the translated outputs. Across nine models, CK reliance is greater for less frequent source words and in sentence contexts that support the supplied meanings. Prompt framing can reduce CK reliance, but seven of nine models favor CK even when explicitly instructed to ignore the supplied meanings. translated_title: 这些程序员熟到能吃了吗？评估大语言模型如何处理翻译中的词汇知识冲突
translated_abstract: 外部词汇资源可以帮助大语言模型（LLM）翻译低资源语言和专业领域的文本，但这些资源可能与模型已有的词汇知识发生冲突。为了隔离这一冲突，我们构建了一个受控的中文到英文翻译任务，为常见的源语言词汇赋予新的含义，这些新含义有的位于相同语义类别之内，有的跨越不同语义类别。我们将提示中提供的这些含义视为情境知识，并系统评估词频、句子语境和提示框架对翻译输出的影响。在九个模型的实验中，模型对情境知识的依赖在源词词频较低、且句子语境支持所提供含义的情况下更为明显。提示框架可以降低模型对情境知识的依赖，但九个模型中有七个即使在被明确指示忽略所提供含义时，仍然偏好情境知识。在同一模型家族内，较大的模型比较小的模型更倾向于在输出中利用情境知识。
tldr: 本研究通过受控的中文-英文翻译任务系统评估了大语言模型在面对外部词汇资源与自身词汇知识冲突时的表现，发现模型（尤其是更大的模型）倾向于依赖提示中提供的情境知识，即使被明确要求忽略这些信息。
en_tdlr: Through a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation task, this study systematically evaluates how LLMs handle conflicts between external lexical resources and their prior lexical knowledge, finding that models—especially larger ones—tend to rely on prompt-supplied contextual knowledge even when explicitly instructed to ignore it.
